text:
evan: Quick company-wide FYI — coordinated SDK + docs announcement for the Eval surface. TL;DR: were promoting the new eval-client v1 (opt-in) today, introducing a stricter eval-result schema, and publishing a 120-day deprecation timeline for the legacy eval HTTP endpoints. This impacts teams running automated evals; Hosted inference remains unchanged.

rita: Short summary of breaking bits?

evan: Two main developer-facing changes:
- New eval-result schema (eval_v2) tightens how metrics & traces are serialized. Old payloads still accepted by the adaptor but will be logged and rate-limited after 120 days.
- eval-client SDK: new package `redwood-eval` (py/js) with improved test harness, local replay mode, and a lightweight CLI. Its opt-in for the first 30 days.

chris: Does eval_v2 change metric names or just structure?

evan: Mostly structure. Metric names are stable but nested under `metrics.{category}.{name}` now (was flat). We also add an explicit `schema_version` field and a more constrained `trace` object (no raw exec strings).

luke: Migration recipe? codemod?

evan: Migration guide published: https://docs.redwood.ai/evals/migrate. Quick python example in "Quick migration":
```python
# legacy
payload = {"accuracy": 0.92, "latency_ms": 120}
# v2
payload = {"schema_version": "eval_v2", "metrics": {"accuracy": {"value": 0.92}, "latency_ms": {"value": 120}}, "trace": {"steps": []}}
client.send_eval(payload)
```
Were providing a codemod (py/js) and a replay harness to validate converted payloads locally.

docs-bot: docs deploy done (deploy-2026-03-25-07) — eval migration guide: https://docs.redwood.ai/evals/migrate :white_check_mark:

ops: Any runtime or infra risk if teams flip to eval-client?

erita: No runtime change for hosted inference. For eval ingest were running the adaptor as a sidecar for 120 days to accept both shapes. We will enable sampling of malformed v1 payloads after 30 days for telemetry and will rate-limit very noisy legacy clients after 90 days.

chris: Security/privacy note? old eval traces sometimes include verbose inputs.

evan: Good call. Eval-client defaults to scrub sensitive fields; docs describe allowed traces. Weve added a new server-side scrubber that removes long raw text from traces unless explicitly opted-in via enterprise config. Security and compliance vetted the changes.

luke: Support comms?

evan: Draft blurb for customer comms: "We're releasing an improved eval client and a stricter eval-result schema (eval_v2) to make metric ingestion more reliable and safer. Legacy eval endpoints will be supported for 120 days; migration tools and a replay harness are available." Use that as-is or shorten.

rita: Action items:
- eng: ship redwood-eval packages and codemod links (rita + chris)
- docs: add per-language quick-checklist and replay howto (docs team)
- ops: monitor eval.adaptor.* metrics and malformed.payload.count (ops)
- support: KB and canned replies for customers who hit rate limits (luke)

luke: I'll prepare the KB and sample email template.

chris: I'll open the codemod PR and attach a small example repo we can run through the replay harness.

evan: Timeline: today - docs deploy & opt-in eval-client release; 30 days - telemetry sampling of legacy payloads; 90 days - start soft rate-limits for noisy legacy clients; 120 days - strict rate-limiting and sunset plan review.

ops: We'll add dashboards and alerts for malformed.payload.count. Also request to surface high-volume clients so support can reach out early.

evan: Agreed. We'll add a per-customer high-volume tag and create a support workflow.

docs-bot: pinned this thread to #announcements for 72h

evan: Thanks all. Please escalate any large customer breakages immediately. :rocket:
